rootText: New To Workforce Getting your first pay cheque is exciting, but it's also the perfect moment to begin planning your future with intention. By laying a strong foundation of protection and financial planning now, you can build a secure future with greater ease. Contact us Lay The Groundwork For Your Best Years Plan for a brighter tomorrow by prioritising the things that matter most to you. Protection MEDIUM PRIORITY In the event of unexpected circumstances such as critical illnesses, accidents or disability, your needs and livelihood might be affected. Your priority for protection: Health insurance for hospitalisation. Protection against accidents and major illnesses so that your needs during recovery continue to be met. Financial payout for death, terminal illness, and total and permanent disability. Plan your protection Wealth MEDIUM PRIORITY Saving for and investing in your upcoming milestones are easier the earlier you start. Your priority for wealth: Savings for future expenses such as home purchase and marriage. Retirement planning. Build your wealth Learn More About Your Needs Protection Wealth Protection The younger you get insured, the better. Now that you've started earning, saving for the things that matter will be much easier without worrying about medical bills. What you already have1 If you are a Singaporean or PR, you’re automatically covered by three national schemes: MediSave A national savings scheme which helps CPF members save for future medical expenses, especially during retirement. MediShield Life A health insurance for large hospital bills and selected outpatient treatment costs. CareShield Life Long-term care insurance scheme for financial support and monthly cash payouts in event of severe disability. What you may consider2 Beyond the basic coverage from national schemes, you’ll still need to ensure that you are sufficiently covered to avoid dipping into any hard-earned savings. National schemes do not fully cover: Hospitalisation An Integrated Shield Plan (IP) provides additional coverage for private hospitals or higher ward classes in public hospitals. Critical Illness You’ll need coverage of 4x annual income. (Recommended)3 Death & Total and Permanent Disability You’ll need coverage of 9 – 10x annual income. (Recommended)3 Make sure your insurance premiums fit comfortably within your budget. It’s recommended to spend at most 15% of take-home pay on insurance protection. Why Act Now Premiums increase as you get older2. Less likely of pre-existing conditions that could exclude you from coverage2. Connect with a Financial Representative for personalised coverage. Contact us Misconceptions? Let’s correct them. Check out some common misunderstandings about financial planning and their truths. Having health insurance means all treatments are fully covered. Health insurance is only for old people. I am young and healthy, I don’t need insurance. Misconception: Having health insurance means all treatments are fully covered. Truth: Not always. Policies can have limits, gaps, and exclusions. It's a good idea to review your coverage, spot any gaps, and consider extra insurance or add-ons based on your health and family history to avoid unexpected medical bills. Source: Health insurance terms: Know what you’re paying for, Moneysense Yes, I want an expert’s help Misconception: Health insurance is only for old people. Truth: Health issues and accidents can happen to anyone at any age. While older people might be more prone to certain illnesses, it's important for everyone to have health insurance. If you wait until you're older, insurers might exclude pre-existing conditions. Protect yourself by getting coverage early on. Source: Understanding Health Insurance, Moneysense Yes, I want an expert’s help Misconception: I am young and healthy, I don’t need insurance. Truth: While this is true, it is also true that health issues can arise at any time, regardless of age. It’s also wise to lock in a lower premium at a younger age.* Yes, I want an expert’s help Find The Right Plan Medical & Accident Critical Illness Whole & Term Life Be protected against unforeseen medical expenses, rising healthcare costs or unexpected injuries with our suite of tailored products and supplementary plans. PRUShield and PRUExtra Comprehensive health insurance coverage to suit your budget and needs. PRUPersonal Accident Personal accident insurance to cover minor mishaps or unexpected injuries even when you’re overseas. Be protected from the financial impact of serious conditions such as cancer, stroke, and heart attack, so you can recover with peace of mind and continue supporting your family in the event of a critical illness. PRUActive Crisis Guard Be covered against health crises that require serious treatments. PRUCancer 360 An affordable cancer insurance plan that provides multi-stage coverage against all cancers. All Critical Illness Plans Get comprehensive essential coverage no matter the life stage you’re at. PRUActive Life V A lifelong promise of protection – strengthened by multiplied coverage and comprehensive critical illness protection. PRUActive LinkGuard An affordable and flexible investment-linked whole life insurance plan that gives you double coverage against unexpected events. PRUActive Term A unique and customisable term insurance plan designed to keep up with your changing needs. This is the first health insurance you should be getting. story Imagine living in a world without insurance Wealth Building your wealth early on is crucial as you’ll need to plan for the big-ticket items of tomorrow. Let your money work for you while you focus on the things that matter to you. Basics – what you should have3 Emergency Funds At least 3 – 6 months’ worth of expenses (including dependants) for rainy days. What you may consider Savings for your upcoming expenses and a plan for you to live out your golden years comfortably – the earlier you start, the more time you have to grow your wealth and accumulate more. Investments It is recommended to allocate at least 10%3 of your take-home pay for key milestones. A Retirement Plan3 It is never too early to start building your nest egg for the retirement lifestyle you want, including monthly payouts. Why Act Now The earlier you start, the longer time horizon you’ll have to accumulate wealth due to the compounding effect4. As lifespans are increasing5, you’ll need a plan for your financial needs in the future. Connect with a Financial Representative for personalised coverage. Contact us Misconceptions? Let’s correct them. Check out some common misunderstandings about financial planning and their truths. I’m too young to start investing. Investing is for the rich. Investing is risky. Misconception: I’m too young to start investing. Truth: Not at all! In fact, starting younger gives you a more generous margin for error. Data shows that the longer your time horizon is, the greater your odds of having stronger returns. Source: Whether You’re Aged 20 or 50, Here’s How You Can Start Investing Amid Uncertainty, The Straits Times, 28 August 2022 Yes, I want an expert’s help Misconception: Investing is for the rich. Truth: There are plenty of investment options that don’t involve huge capital amounts. You may start small by investing some of your first few pay cheques in options that may require lower capital amounts and are aligned with your needs. The key is to be consistent and think long-term! Yes, I want an expert’s help Misconception: Investing is risky. Truth: Investing does come with some risk, but there are ways to manage it. You can balance risk and potential returns by diversifying your investments and choosing lower-risk assets. Understanding your own risk tolerance and considering your financial commitments are also important in reducing investment risk. Source: Managing Investment Risk, Moneysense Yes, I want an expert’s help Find The Right Plan Savings Investments Achieve your life goals at any life stage and gain financial security and the freedom to live out your best years.
